👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: New intro text claims a finished scan and a Fix all plan in every idle state**

`reconcileIntro` now reads "Kaipu compared this folder with your library. Here's what Fix all would do…". `reconcile-dialog.tsx:431` renders it whenever `run.phase === "idle"`, so it also shows above "Checking your folder…" while the scan runs, above `reconcileScanError` and the busy/already-running messages, and above "Everything matches." In none of those states has a comparison finished, and none has a Fix all plan to show. The old wording ("Kaipu compares your folder…") was true in all of them. Fix: render this sentence only when `scan.status === "ok" && scan.findings.length > 0`, or go back to wording that works in every state. Separately, "grouped by what's wrong" doesn't match how the code groups findings: `GROUP_OF` groups by what happens to each one (the comment at reconcile-dialog.tsx:105-107 says so), and the Spanish text says "agrupado por lo que pasa". Apply the same fix to es.json:812.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "Gone" group header doesn't fit two of the rows it holds**

`GROUP_OF` puts `orphan-companion` and cloud-only `missing-media` (vault-reconcile.ts:471-481, `action: "cloud-only"`) in the `gone` group. Its header says "In the library, but the file is gone" / "Set aside in the orphans folder". An orphan companion isn't in the library, and a cloud-only record isn't set aside: it stays in the library. The body text and the per-row notes do correct this, but the collapsed header, which is the part people read first, says the opposite for those rows. Consider a more general action line (for example "Set aside, or kept as cloud only"), or a title that covers Kaipu files with no item.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test name promises row text but only counts list items**

The test "every finding kind lands in a group with its own row text" only checks the group order and the `li` count per group (line 245). It never checks any row's text, so a kind that rendered an empty or wrong note would still pass. Either check each row's note or rename the test to what it actually checks.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

The new intro ("Kaipu compared this folder… Here's what Fix all would do") and the `SafetyNote` render in every idle state, not only when there is a list. While scanning, the past-tense "compared" sits over "Checking your folder…". On a busy/error result or "Everything matches.", it promises a Fix all preview that never comes. The old intro was worded to fit every state. When there are only listed findings, it also promises a Fix all that isn't offered.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Intro + safety note shown in states where they don't apply

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/library/reconcile/reconcile-dialog.tsx:431-432 — `reconcileIntro` and `<SafetyNote>` render whenever `run.phase === "idle"`, independent of `scanning` / `scan.status` / `scan.findings.length`.
- packages/i18n/messages/en.json:812, es.json:812 — `reconcileIntro` copy is now specific to the "ok with findings" state.

## Required outcome
- The "Here's what Fix all would do" intro and the safety note only appear when a findings list is shown (`scan.status === "ok"` and `findings.length > 0`), or the intro copy is reworded so it reads correctly in the scanning / busy / error / everything-matches states too.

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Move the intro + `SafetyNote` into `ScanBody`'s `"ok"` branch next to `<Findings>`, keeping a neutral line (or none) for the other states.
````

</details>

"grouped by what's wrong" describes the old split, not this one. The groups are named for what Fix all does to the files ("Renamed to match the title", "Added to the library", …), and the Spanish string already says "agrupado por lo que pasa". English could say "grouped by what happens to each file" so both locales match the cards.

**Remove the 200-row cap, or make the group list scrollable without a cap, so every fixable finding has its own selection control.** When a group has more than 200 fixable findings, the rows after the first 200 render only as an overflow count. Those findings have no individual checkbox. Their selection can change only through the group checkbox, which also changes the displayed findings. `Fix all` sends every path not in `skipped`, so an overflow finding is fixed unless the whole group is unticked. The row cap conflicts with the comment at the group body, which states that hundreds of files scroll inside their group. Render every finding in the group. The group body already scrolls, so no other layout change is required.

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: `skipPaths` validates renderer input but no test covers it**

`skipPaths` is the only check on the new `skip` value that the renderer sends to the main process. It drops non-arrays and non-string entries. It is exported, but nothing in `src/` imports or tests it, so the guarantee in its comment ("a malformed payload skips nothing rather than failing the run") is not pinned. A short unit test would cover `undefined`, a non-array, and a mixed array such as `["a", 1, null]` → `{"a"}`.
